page.layout: One page of text, no margin notes. Printed page number 79 at top right. Heading in capitals with a Greek word, then one verse poem in five stanzas, set in a single column. Decorated initial S at the start of the poem.

main_text.head: AD FRANCISCUM OLIVARIUM FRANCIÆ Cancellarium, εὐχαριστήριον[?].
main_text.p: SI quod sub antro Castalio latet Carmen repositum, quod sera robora, Quod saxa ducat fluminūmque Præcipites remoretur undas: Nunc prome sacri Calliope Chori Regina, Olivarii & memora piam Mentem Camœnarum erga alumnos, Et memori refer ore grates: Qui, quanquam ab alto culmine Gallicæ Rei gubernet munia publicæ, & A rege permissas habenas Imperio moderetur æquo, Nec fasci iniquo subditus ingemit, Nec re secunda turgidus intumet, Utraque fortuna peraque Infragilisque animique rectus[?]. Interque curæ pondera publicæ Martisque vix dum compositi minas, Non negligit ceu se minores Vulgi humiles tenuis querelas.

page.notes: Show-through of the reverse page (mirrored "VARIA POEMATA" and other mirrored lines at top and right) is not transcribed. No running head, catchword or signature is printed on this page. The initial S is a woodcut and is joined to "I quod" as "SI quod". Doubtful readings: the Greek word in the heading and "rectus" at the end of line 4 of the fourth stanza.
